name: Costa Brava Holm Oak Forest
description: Mediterranean holm oak forest: 11 agents from the mycorrhizal network (keystone) to raptors and the coastal tourism economy; Fire & Microclimate Regulation degrades exponentially past the threshold, and three edges into Understory & Matorral are rescaled to the in-degree cap (Step 3.8). Small losses are priced linearly (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1). Illustrative. Derivations: gaia/cases/definitions/CASE_NOTES.md.

units_per_ha.note: Chosen so the per-tree absorption gives ~1.8 t CO2/ha/yr.

unit_value.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
unit_value.note: Revenue per holm oak felled (one-off). Rated Medium in the case docstring, but no market source is cited.

safe_threshold_ratio.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
safe_threshold_ratio.note: Safe extraction threshold, lower than temperate forest for drought and fire (stated rationale, no cited source); under the area_loss damage model (Step 8d.1) the depletion beyond which the REMAINING resource starts to degrade; below it each hectare lost costs its average value.

agent[*].dependency_weight.source: owner specification (case docstring), no external source
agent[*].dependency_weight.note: Rated Medium in the case docstring; an expert judgement with no cited source.

edge[*].strength.note: Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia's): x0.5 to x1.5, a judgement for unfitted strengths, narrower than the placeholder x/÷3 that put almost every draw above the in-degree cap. Edges into an agent whose incoming strengths (keystone boosts included) exceed 1/1.5 of the cap rise at most to the cap: see their own range.

annual_value_per_ha.source: de Groot et al. (2012), Ecosystem Services 1:50-61, doi:10.1016/j.ecoser.2012.07.005, Table 2 (read in full): woodlands, total economic value Int$1,588/ha/yr minus climate regulation Int$7 = Int$1,581/ha/yr (2007 international dollars, 2007 price level; 21 estimates, Table 3); converted to EUR with the World Bank's PPP conversion factor for household final consumption (PA.NUS.PRVT.PP, the 'private consumption' series de Groot et al. used), Spain, 2007: 0.808165 EUR per international $ (World Development Indicators, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ESP/indicator/PA.NUS.PRVT.PP?date=2007&format=json, read 13 October 2026; gaia/currency.py)
annual_value_per_ha.note: Every agent; the dependency weights split it. Step 8g.6 (the owner's answer: convert international dollars to euros everywhere): 1,581 x 0.808165 = EUR 1,277.71/ha/yr in 2007 euros at Spanish purchasing power (it was used at face value as EUR 1,593, from figures partly typed from memory: 1,600 - 7; now read in Table 2). Not inflated to a later price year and no income adjustment (Step 8d.5). Climate regulation is left out (carbon is valued only by gaia.carbon, decision D3). A global woodland mean, not a Mediterranean holm-oak valuation.

steepness.note: Degradation of the REMAINING resource past the safe threshold (damage model area_loss, Step 8d.1, as for Posidonia): zero up to the threshold, then a logistic with its inflection 15% into the post-threshold span, the same curve for every agent except Fire & Microclimate Regulation. The damage of each agent is D + (1 - D) x degradation, so its slope at small losses is exactly 1 (each hectare lost costs its average value) and the curve shapes only the threshold behaviour. Not fitted to field data (calibration regime B). Monte Carlo range 6-18, uniform (Step 8e.4, as Posidonia: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 gave 4-36).

base.note: Degradation of Fire & Microclimate Regulation past the safe threshold (area_loss, Step 8d.1): zero up to the threshold, then exponential over the post-threshold span (fire feedback, no plateau): (base^((D - t)/(1 - t)) - 1)/(base - 1); not fitted to fire data. Monte Carlo range 1.5-3 (x0.75 to x1.5, Step 8e.4): the base must stay above 1 for a growing curve, and the placeholder x/÷3 (0.67-6) put a third of the draws at or below 1, which validation rejects.

agents.name: Mycorrhizal Fungi
agents.description: Keystone underground network — nutrient/water transport, cascades to all tree regeneration

keystone_threshold.note: Health below which the agent's outgoing edges double; hand-set, no source. Monte Carlo range 0.15-0.45, uniform (Step 8e.4, Posidonia's +-0.15: a judgement; the placeholder x/÷3 reached 0.9-1.0, where the keystone boost would fire at almost any damage).

agents.name: Canopy Trees

strength.note: Hand-set placeholder strength. Monte Carlo range (Step 8e.4): x0.5 to x1.176. The incoming strengths into Canopy Trees sum to 0.850 of the in-degree cap of 1 (keystone boosts included), so the edges into it can rise only by x1.176 together before a draw breaks the cap; their documented values are therefore the top of their range (x1.176), not its middle. Drawn values are never rescaled.
